title_original: Hungry for action? Our critics’ verdicts on the week’s UK cinema releases
excerpt_original: A Hunger Games cash-grab, up close with Elizabeth Holmes, Helen Mirren plays Patricia Highsmith, and Maradona’s helping hand … here are all the latest film releases at a glance *** Continue reading...

blocks.text: You Can See Everything ★★★★★

blocks.alt: Elizabeth Holmes, closeup, with tousled blond hair, smiling slightly while looking to the side
blocks.caption: Intense … Elizabeth Holmes in You Can See Everything. Photograph: A24

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Intense close-range study of Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim attempts to get to grips with whether or not she believes the truth of what she says.

What our reviewer said “Holmes clearly believes that faking it and making it are the same thing. Fielder is fascinated and suspicious at her evasive, ersatz-childlike failure to grasp what he is asking her, yet she appears also genuinely to lack a sense of truth and falsehood.” Peter Bradshaw
Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother ★★★☆☆

blocks.alt: Latif holds baby Fatiha facing a woman, as Qadir reads on the floor in a sunlit living room
blocks.caption: Mahershala Ali as Latif in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. Photograph: Amazon Content Services LLC/PA

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Mahershala Ali plays a devout Muslim contract killer on the hunt for baby milk in a blackly comic thriller with shades of Tarantino and John Woo.

What our reviewer said “The movie is boisterous and frenetic, well acted by Ali and everyone else and interestingly shot in dense, saturated colour by cinematographer Katelin Arizmendi.” Peter Bradshaw
Josephine ★★★☆☆

blocks.alt: Claire embraces young Josephine, who rests her chin on her shoulder with a pensive expression
blocks.caption: The lead performance is outstanding … Gemma Chan, Mason Reeves and Channing Tatum in Josephine. Photograph: Curzon/PA

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan play the parents of a young child who witnesses a sex assault in Beth de Araújo’s knotty drama.
What our reviewer said “I was unsure about some of the film’s high-concept ideas but the lead performance from its eight-year-old newcomer Mason Reeves is outstanding.” Peter Bradshaw
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ★☆☆☆☆

blocks.alt: A young man with curly blond hair kneels in a forest in a Hunger Games film still
blocks.caption: Joseph Zada and McKenna Grace in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. Photograph: Capital Pictures/Alamy

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Second prequel to the hit future-dystopia death-match saga, with Joseph Zada as 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy, who will go on to be Katniss Everdeen’s mentor.
What our reviewer said “This film has no actual interest and no authentic reason to exist, other than to gouge an income stream out of its fanbase.” Peter Bradshaw
Heysel 85 ★★★★☆

blocks.alt: At the Heysel Stadium disaster, a woman in a teal dress stands amid fallen, injured people
blocks.caption: Heysel 85. Photograph: Toon Aerts

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Reconstruction of the grim sequence of bad judgments that led to 39 fans dying in the Heysel stadium before the European cup final in 1985.

What our reviewer said “The roar of the crowd echoing overhead through the stadium’s claustrophobic tunnels is like the wailing of the damned, while the sport’s officer class flinch and panic as if at a wartime loss.” Peter Bradshaw
Filipiñana ★★★★☆

blocks.alt: A girl with bangs sits holding a golf club, viewed between a nearby person’s legs
blocks.caption: To a tee … Filipiñana. Photograph: BFI Distribution

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Menacing Philippines-set satire on class and privilege via a verdant private golf course in water-deprived Manila, peopled with submissive tee-girls and geisha-style caddies.
What our reviewer said “The film is a coolly controlled, mesmeric midsummer day’s daydream of menace.” Peter Bradshaw
American Doctor ★★★★☆

blocks.alt: Dr Feroze Sidhwa and colleagues in surgical masks lean closely together during an operation
blocks.caption: Powerful … American Doctor. Photograph: courtesy of Watermelon Pictures

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Documentary by former ABC News executive Poh Si Teng that follows three doctors from the US who sign up to volunteer at the Nasser hospital in Gaza during the Israeli military assault.
What our reviewer said “It’s a powerful, angry film, in a state of despair at the scale of suffering and devastation.” Cath Clarke
My Wife Cries ★★★★☆

blocks.alt: A shirtless man with a towel stands near others outdoors amid trees and plants
blocks.caption: My Wife Cries. Photograph: Cinema Guild

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Famously austere German director Angela Schanelec offers a sometimes playful study of everyday emotional turmoil as a marriage falls apart.

What our reviewer said “There’s an enigmatic blend of theatricality and cinematic wizardry here, with wordy contemplations often occurring when characters are on the move, walking, cycling or simply wandering about.” Phuong Le
The Nice Ones ★★★☆☆

blocks.alt: A closeup from The Nice Ones of a pale, startled face with a bloody forehead wound
blocks.caption: Ominous vibes … The Nice Ones. Photograph: RG Films

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Unsettling tale of unbalanced minds and Unidentified Aerial Phenomena from Peter Stylianou, where aliens turn people into grinning body hosts.

What our reviewer said “The Nice Ones drums up enough ominous vibes to remain watchable throughout and there are even a few moments when it seems as though it is in thrall to the pulpy spirit of vintage John Carpenter.” Phil Hoad
The Match ★★★☆☆

blocks.alt: Maradona shakes hands with Shilton between referees before the 1986 World Cup quarter-final
blocks.caption: Infamous … Maradona and Peter Shilton shake hands in a still from The Match. Photograph: Goodfellas

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Co-directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco bring England and Argentina players together for a look back at the infamous “hand of God” clash during the 1986 football World Cup.
What our reviewer said “The main sense here is of a film looking for a spirit of reconciliation, and a final contest over a table football game suggests they may well have found it.” Andrew Pulver
Madden ★★☆☆☆

blocks.alt: Christian Bale and Nicolas Cage as John Madden point fists forward on a stadium field
blocks.caption: Game on … Christian Bale and Nicolas Cage in Madden. Photograph: Chuck Zlotnick/Prime/AP

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Nicolas Cage stars as a cartoonish version of NFL coach John Madden, in a biopic from David O Russell.

What our reviewer said “Madden is close to a Pop Tarts movie version of the formidable coach’s story, reducing one of the 20th century’s most celebrated pop culture figures to a thin caricature.” Andrew Lawrence
A Talent for Murder ★★★☆☆

blocks.alt: Helen Mirren as Patricia Highsmith, holding her head with a troubled expression at a desk
blocks.caption: The Talented Ms Mirren … A Talent for Murder. Photograph: Universal Pictures/PA

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence A fictionalised version of cantankerous crime author Patricia Highsmith, played by Helen Mirren , plots a murder with an ambitious editor.
What our reviewer said “We’re being led down a road of twists and turns but none really jolt or surprise as much as we expect, the rug never really being pulled, just gently tugged at.” Benjamin Lee
